description.cancellation_policy:
Cancellation Policy:  There is a $36 non-refundable reservation fee. User fees are refunded if you cancel more than 7 days in advance of your launch date.

Change Policy: You may change group size or trip length up until 7 days prior to your launch date. Additional fees may apply. You may list one alternate trip leader at the time of booking. You may NOT change the trip start date at any time or make any changes once you print the permit. However, you may cancel and rebook.

If you have booked the wrong type of permit (Ex. entry point "Flatwater" instead of "Cataract Canyon"), you will need to cancel the incorrect permit and book a new one. We will not refund the $36 fee in these cases. Be sure you have read all the Need to know information and have booked the correct permit before completing payment.
description.comment_box_description: This permit reservation is only for the portion of your trip within Canyonlands National Park (below Potash or Mineral Bottom Boat Ramps), if your full trip starts somewhere else (i.e. Green River State Park) please provide the date and location here. If doing a Flatwater trip, enter which company you have made reservations with for an up-river shuttle (see Need to Know below).  If other (i.e. hiking out, personal motorboat) describe your route.  Note, you will need a separate permit from the BLM for the Green River above Mineral Bottom.
description.description:
Canyonlands National Park is a wilderness of countless canyons and fantastically formed buttes carved by the Colorado River and its tributaries. Rivers divide the park into four districts: Island in the Sky, The Needles, The Maze, and the rivers themselves. The park preserves the natural beauty and human history throughout its four districts. While they share a primitive desert atmosphere, each offers different opportunities for wildness and solitude.

The Colorado and Green Rivers have played a significant role in shaping the landscape of Canyonlands. Seeing the park from the bottom up affords a unique perspective. Above their confluence at the heart of Canyonlands, the rivers offer miles of flatwater perfect for canoes, sea kayaks and other shallow-water boats. A commercial upriver shuttle is necessary for non-motorized boats. Below the confluence, the combined flow of both rivers spills down Cataract Canyon with remarkable speed and power, creating a fourteen-mile stretch of Class III to V whitewater. Cataract Canyon is a particularly hazardous and isolated section of the Colorado River, subject to extreme water level fluctuations, for experienced river runners only. 

There are numerous options for responsible camping prior to your Canyonlands National Park river trip. Visit Discover Moab for options in the Moab area.

description.fee_policy:
Permit Reservation Fee: There is a non-refundable, $36.00 reservation fee for all permit reservations.

Recreation Fee: $25 per person

Entrance Fee: The park charges an entrance fee which you may pay upon arrival or purchase in advance. The park also honors valid annual or lifetime America the Beautiful-the National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Passes (e.g. Senior, Military, 4th Grade, etc.) also known as interagency passes. For more information visit the park's Fees & Passes web page.
description.need_to_know_email:
This is a confirmation email, not the permit.

Your permit will be available on your Recreation.gov account to print (or download) 7 days prior to your launch date. Contact the Backcountry Permit Office (email canyres@nps.gov or call 435-241-3110) if you need your permit issued early. The permit must be in the Trip Leader’s possession at all times.

If your launch date is within 7 days, log into your Recreation.gov account to issue and print (or download) your permit.

Review the following information:

  • Boat Ramps: The North Wash Boat Ramp is the closest takeout after Cataract Canyon. Recent improvements have been made to this ramp. Familiarize yourself with the changes before taking out here. Read about additional launch points and takeouts in the park’s Boating Information Guide. Check Glen Canyon's Changing Lake Levels for current ramp conditions. 

  • Labyrinth Canyon: For trips starting upstream of Mineral Bottom (Labyrinth Canyon), a separate permit from the Moab BLM Field Office. is required,

  • Change Policy: Be sure all your information is correct before issuing. Changes cannot be made once your permit is issued. The launch date cannot be changed.

  • Required Video: You and all participants agree to watch the Flatwater and/or Cataract Canyon videos.

  • Required Equipment: You are responsible for reviewing and complying with the park's River Regulations which include mandatory equipment and other important requirements.

  • Entrance Fee. Please pay in advance or bring a valid pass (e.g. Senior, Military, 4th Grade, etc.).
description.need_to_know_order:
Contact the Backcountry Permit Office with questions or to receive your permit early by phone: 435-241-3110 or email: CANYres@nps.gov

Before you continue: 

  • Your entry date is the day you will be launching from/passing by Mineral Bottom or Potash boat ramp. Do not add the launch date from somewhere further upstream (e.g., Ruby Ranch). This permit is valid only within Canyonlands. You need a separate permit from the BLM to float the Green River above Mineral Bottom.

  • Changes can be made to reservations with some exceptions. Alternate trip leaders and launch dates cannot be changed. Once issued, no changes are allowed. However, you may cancel and rebook. Fees apply.

  • Book an upriver jet-boat shuttle BEFORE you book this permit for non-motorized flatwater trips. Park-authorized jet-boat shuttle providers: Tex’s Riverways Canyonlands By Night and Day

  • Cataract Canyon is a challenging stretch of river at all water levels, for experienced boaters only. You and all participants must watch the required Flatwater and Cataract Canyon videos.

  • Review the park's Boating Information Guide for camping, motorized boat registration, equipment, aquatic invasive species requirements and more.

You must print or download your permit before you launch. Bring all pages with you. Your permit is available 7 days in advance of your launch date via your recreation.gov account.

The trip leader is responsible for ensuring all participants know and abide by River Regulations including mandatory equipment (flotation devices, trash and human waste disposal, etc.) and other important requirements.

The takeout for Cataract Canyon is on Lake Powell. Low lake water levels make takeout difficult. Hite Ramp is closed indefinitely. North Wash takeout is an improved dirt and concrete ramp; 4WD vehicles are strongly recommended. Bullfrog Ramp (approximately 50 miles/80 km down lake from North Wash) is available to small vessels.

For current conditions, email CANYres@nps.gov or visit the Changing Lake Levels page.
description.need_to_know_permit:
Who needs an overnight river permit?

A river permit is required for all boat trips on the Green and Colorado Rivers. 

  • This permit is valid for noncommercial groups only. Only park concessionaires are permitted to lead commercial river trips. Contact SEUG_CommercialServices@nps.gov for questions regarding commercial use and guiding in the park.

  • Academic institutions may require a Special Use Permit for river trips. Please visit the Academic River Trips web page for instructions.  

  • If you would like to bring a church group, activity- based club, or other organized group on the River, please contact the Backcountry Permit Office (email: canyres@nps.gov phone: ((435) 241-3110) before booking your permit. 

BEFORE YOU RESERVE YOUR PERMIT:

Ensure you are booking the correct permit. Select "Cataract Canyon" as your entry point if you plan to run rapids. All other trips select "Flatwater".

Review the Canyonlands Boating Information Guide and River Regulations which specify mandatory equipment, requirements for human waste disposal, PFDs, Food/Trash Storage and disposal, campfires and more.

Review the information on the web pages listed below and watch the mandatory video(s). If you plan to boat through Cataract Canyon, also read the Flatwater web page and watch the Flatwater video.

  • Flatwater. 

  • Cataract Canyon. is a challenging stretch of river at all water levels and is only recommended for experienced boaters. If you have any questions or concerns, contact the Backcountry Permit Office. Trips through Cataract Canyon must cross a portion of Lake Powell to reach the takeout. The location where the river ends and the lake begins varies throughout the year. Given the distances involved and the frequency of strong, up-canyon winds, motors are recommended. Read more about take outs in the Boating Information Guide.  

  • Packrafts  

    • If you are accessing the river corridor on foot and plan to only float on flatwater you may select ‘Packraft: Night on the River’ for the nights spent in the river corridor. These are located under our land based permits.

    • If your itinerary starts on a trail and you are boating whitewater, you must obtain a Canyonlands Overnight River Permit and select the entry point "Cataract Canyon".

    • Wildlife closures may apply.

For more trip planning information, visit the Boating page or contact the Backcountry Permit Office (email: canyres@nps.gov phone: (435) 259-4351).

OTHER THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE YOU BOOK A RESERVATION:

  • These permits are only valid within Canyonlands National Park (downstream of the Potash and Mineral Bottom Boat Ramps). If you are launching upstream (e.g., Ruby Ranch), the start date for your Canyonlands permit should be the day you will enter Canyonlands National Park.

  • You will need a separate BLM permit for the Green River above Mineral Bottom boat ramp. River maps are available from the Canyonlands Park Store. Read more about launch points in the park’s Boating Information Guide.

  • The Island in the Sky Visitor Center does not issue River permits.

During checkout, complete the “Comments” field:

  • If your full trip starts somewhere above Potash or Mineral Bottom Boat Ramps (e.g., Green River State Park), enter the launch date and location. 

  • If you select a flatwater trip with the Exit Point "Spanish Bottom Upriver Shuttle," then enter the name of the jet boat shuttle company,  

  • If you select a a flatwater trip and you plan to exit other than via jet boat shuttle (e.g., hike out, personal motorboat), enter the explanation. 

You may not change a trip start date once you book a reservation. However, you may cancel and rebook the reservation. Alternate trip leaders can only be designated when you book the permit. They cannot be added or changed after the permit is reserved.  

You may book a reservation up to 3 days before the launch date. There are no daily launch limits. In-Station permits are also available in person at the Backcountry Office, 2282 Resource Blvd, Moab, UT 84532.

Jet-Boat Shuttle. Non-motorized, flatwater trips on the Green or Colorado River must obtain a commercial upriver jet-boat shuttle from Spanish Bottom prior to making a reservation.

Park authorized shuttle operators:  

  • Tex’s Riverways 

  • Canyonlands By Night and Day 

Motorized Boat Requirements. Motorized boats must be registered, including those from out-of-state. Motorized boats must have valid state registration, decals, placards, and a serviceable fire extinguisher. Boats with out-of-state registration may boat on Utah waters for 60 days per calendar year (boats must have hull numbers). 

  • Before launching your boat for Cataract Canyon, be aware of Utah state law for Aquatic Invasive Species in Utah (such as Quagga mussels). 

  • Personal Flotation Devices (PFDs) must be worn below North Wash and Hite.

Camping along the rivers. Rivers usually reach peak flows in early May to late June. Water flows recede throughout the summer and reach low flows in the fall months. Sandbars make great campsites at low flows while campsites can be difficult to find at high flows. Some rapids are most difficult at higher flows, while other become more difficult at lower flows.  

  • Camping below the confluence. Camping areas are first-come, first-served. However, on the east bank of the Colorado below the confluence (mile 214.3) look for the sign warning of rapids ahead. At the base of the sign is a campsite registration box. Groups camping below the confluence are urged to indicate which campsites they intend to use so that other boaters may plan their stops in advance. This applies to both flatwater groups meeting their jet-boat shuttle as well as groups continuing down Cataract Canyon. This system is simply a courtesy to others and does not guarantee a campsite. Please do not sign up groups other than your own. 

  • Camping on the upper reaches of Lake Powell (below Imperial Canyon and above Hite) are limited, unreliable, and constantly changing with the water levels.
description.no_show_policy:
No Show Policy:

If the permit is not printed by 8:00 AM on the launch date, the entire river permit will be canceled. You may be contacted by our reservations office to confirm.
description.quota_details:
There are no daily launch limits.

Non-motorized flatwater trips on the Green or Colorado River must obtain a commercial upriver shuttle from Spanish Bottom prior to making a reservation. Do not make a reservation if you have not reserved a shuttle. Park concession operators are:

  • Tex’s Riverways 

  • Canyonlands By Night and Day
description.season_information:
Permits are required year-round. A permit allows the launch of one group (max. 40 people) on the date selected to camp in the river corridor up to 14 days. If you plan to run the rapids in Cataract Canyon select "Cataract Canyon" as your Entry Point. If you do not, select Flatwater.

  • Permits are available in advance. See "Important Dates". Permits are released at 8:00 am MST

  • ALL non-motorized, Flatwater boaters must book a commercial upriver shuttle before booking a permit (see "How Does the Quota Work for this Permit?") 

  • Permits are self-issue. You may print or download up to 7 days in advance of your launch date.

  • An alternate trip leader may be entered a the time of booking. This cannot be added or changed at a later time.

  • Once a permit is printed, you cannot make changes. You may cancel and rebook the permit.

  • Advanced permit reservations online close 2 days prior to a launch date. In-station permits are available at the Backcountry Office in Moab during Operating Hours & Seasons.

reminder_details.need_to_know:
Dear Canyonlands National Park River Permit Reservation holder,

Permits are available to print starting 7 days prior to the launch date. Log into your www.recreation.gov account to print your permit. Do not forget to print ALL pages of your permit. In addition to the required river equipment, you must have a signed copy of your permit. Make sure to read over all regulations on the back of the permit prior to signing it. Please cancel your permit reservation if you will not be using it.

Motor Registration:

  • Any boat with a motor must have valid state registration, decals, placards, and a serviceable fire extinguisher.

Mineral Bottom Conditions:

  • Low flows and changes in sediment deposits in the river channel have made launching or taking out from Mineral Bottom difficult and time consuming. Expect to wade through mud at least 3 ft (1 m) deep for a significant distance.

  • Large motorboats maybe not be able to use the ramp unless Flaming Gorge Dam releases raise water levels.

Takeout Information:

  • Hite Ramp: Closed.

  • North Wash (AKA Dirty Devil): The ramp is not for motorized boats or small boat launching. The staging area is small and users must "share the road" when rigging and derigging. The ramp is steep. A 4-wheel drive vehicle is highly recommended to access the river. Please review the map of North Wash before staging.

  • Bullfrog Ramp: If you plan to use Bullfrog Ramp (Glen Canyon NRA), anticipate 10+ hours with a motor to navigate the delta. PFDs are needed and expect sand waves, Class II-III rapids, mud shelves, and shallow water with wood debris.

Low lake water levels will make take-outs for Cataract Canyon challenging. Please check current available ramps on the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area website for up-to-date conditions. We encourage boaters to check the take-out calendar (updated monthly) and collaborate with other users on the river as you approach the lake to work out take-out times. 

Have a safe and enjoyable trip!
